status.comment: consumer-neutral proof surface for any VS Code fork

p.POLYGON-PURPOSE: The polygon is an external patch-set repository plus an external managed VS Code checkout operated by the installed Codkit tool. It is test data, not a consumer product and not content owned by toolRoot.

facts.POLYGON-THREE-ROOTS: toolRoot, polygon patchesDir, and polygon forkDir use unrelated, pairwise-disjoint paths; the run starts from a cwd outside all three.
facts.POLYGON-SETTINGS-PROOF: At least one full run selects both external roots only through a temporary HOME containing strict `~/.codkit/settings.json`; separate runs prove each CLI and environment override independently.
facts.POLYGON-PORTABLE-INPUT: The patch-set describes only its selected fork/pin. No path, identifier, service, feature, or branding from another consumer is required.

p.SAMPLE-PROCEDURE: Each sample is authored in forkDir, extracted or declared in patchesDir, verified, synchronized again from the pin, and inspected through schema-2 inventory/effective diff. Sample ids use a reserved test range in that patch-set.

tr.td: one marker-scoped hook in a stable method; save, byte-stable regeneration, and hunks-inside-markers
one module below `src/vs/<ownDirName>/`, copied both directions without symlinks
one non-bootstrap service with a contract test; installed forbidden list remains effective
one minimal graft or top-level entry, with every fork-specific registry represented by its own attributable artifact
one non-branding configuration key with `expectUpstream`, dev materialization where supported, and build materialization
one small deterministic resource replacement and equality guard
one expected-match rule whose drift is observable
one reversible hide plus removed-registry entry and mandatory guards

p.SAMPLE-COMPLETENESS: Inventory has at least one entry for every intervention layer, all ids and owners are unique/known, every required guard is declared, and completeness explains every generated fork path exactly once.

facts.POLYGON-OLD-PIN: Prepare a branch on an older reachable VS Code pin with a clean, a renamed, and a deliberately conflicting intervention.
facts.POLYGON-CYCLE: Run forecast, cycle start/continue/status, rename handling, classified full red list, required resolution stop, journal completeness, regeneration and final verify on the target pin.
facts.POLYGON-RESUME: Inject interruption at each durable phase boundary and prove a fresh process continues without lost work or duplicate canonical commits.
facts.POLYGON-METRICS: Record the final inventory metrics snapshot in the committed cycle journal; no tool-repository metrics file is required.

facts.POLYGON-AIRGAP: Run verify and, with supplied dependencies, build in a container with physical `--network none`; any attempted network operation is a failure.
facts.POLYGON-UID-READONLY: Exercise foreign UID/safe.directory and read-only mounts: read-only commands work, writes fail before partial mutation, and writable runtime mounts are explicit.
facts.POLYGON-UPSTREAM-BASELINE: Run the selected full upstream/Electron runner baseline, not only focused own tests, and preserve its complete red list as evidence.
facts.POLYGON-PACKAGING: Build/package a distributable bundle and inspect that own, overlay, resource and generated metadata are present in final artifacts, not merely in the development checkout.
facts.POLYGON-NATIVE: Execute the same fixture natively on macOS and Windows, including launchers, Git/path semantics, double regeneration and daemon lifecycle. Linux evidence does not close these rows.

p.POLYGON-READY: The polygon is accepted only when every sample, upgrade/resume proof, air-gap/UID/read-only proof, upstream baseline, packaging proof and native OS row has recorded executable evidence. A missing runner is an explicit open risk, never an implied pass.

generic-polygon.title: 6. The second polygon - synthetic and typeless

p.POLYGON-GENERIC-IS-SYNTHETIC: FEAT-001 becomes **two** polygons (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-ENGINE-TESTS`). The first is the one described in §§1-5: a real fork tree of a `vscode` patch set. The second is the polygon of the `generic` type and is a **synthetic repository in the fixtures** (owner ruling of 2026-09-09) - a small git upstream generated by code, with two pins, no product manifest, no extensions, no service registry and no entry module; its install, lint, compile and test commands are stub scripts declared in `typeConfig`. It costs no external checkout, it runs in the tool's own CI, and it is the standing proof that the engine works without a product model.

p.POLYGON-GENERIC-COVERAGE: What the synthetic polygon must carry: the layers a typeless upstream can have - `own` in a configured directory, `patch` with markers, `resource-file`, `rewrite-rule` and a `config-overlay` over a declared JSON target with no dev channel; the verbs `load`, `save`, `verify`, `cycle`, `publish` against a local bare remote and `ci --profile verify`; and the capability refusals of the verbs the type does not answer (`imageset`, `gen brand`, `build`, `runtime load`), each `CK-E-TYPE-CAPABILITY`. What it deliberately does not carry: brand images, a runtime library, built-in extensions and any upstream-specific build - those are proved on the first polygon alone.

p.POLYGON-GENERIC-IMPL: The P3 implementation: `packages/codkit/test/fixtures/makeGenericUpstream.ts` generates the upstream - a git repository with an ordinary `app.json` manifest, a panel module carrying the anchors of the patch and of the rewrite rule, a helper module edited between the pins, a module deleted between them, a binary logo and stub lint/test scripts - with the pins `v1.0.0` and `v1.1.0` and a fixed author, committer and clock, so the shas are the same on every machine. `packages/codkit/test/fixtures/makeGenericPatchSet.ts` writes the patch set of type `generic`: one artifact per layer a plain upstream has, a `typeConfig` declaring the own root `src/own`, the lint and test commands, the overlay target and the manifest fingerprint, and a patch generated as a real unified diff and checked with `git apply` against the pin. `packages/codkit/test/support/genericFixture.ts` clones the fork tree and runs the shipped launcher, exactly as the first polygon does. The scenarios run in `packages/codkit/test/e2e/genericPolygon.test.ts`. The text machinery both polygons share moved to `packages/codkit/test/fixtures/patchText.ts`.
